target.title: fix: prevent Web Push broadcasts from spiking outbound requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators broadcasting a Web Push notification to many browser or device subscriptions would open every outbound HTTPS push request at once. Large subscription sets could therefore create an avoidable burst of sockets, encryption work, and upstream requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The broadcast now schedules subscription sends through the shared bounded-concurrency worker with a limit of 12 while preserving input order and best-effort per-subscription results. VAPID details are passed per send so overlapping bounded broadcasts cannot overwrite each other's identity, and expired subscriptions are removed in one compare-before-clear state update without deleting a registration refreshed while its old send was in flight.

## User Impact

Web Push broadcasts continue attempting every subscription and cleaning up 404/410 endpoints, but peak outbound send concurrency is now capped. This reduces resource spikes for users with many browser, device, or team subscriptions without adding configuration or changing the payload/API surface.

## Evidence

- Focused local Vitest run of `src/infra/push-web.test.ts`: **14 tests passed**. Coverage includes the 12-send ceiling, complete fan-out, overlapping broadcasts with distinct VAPID identities, compare-before-clear during a subscription refresh, cleanup persistence failure, and mixed 201/404/410 results. The suite also passed with all three VAPID environment variables pre-populated to verify test isolation.
- Local live transport proof invoked the production `broadcastWebPush()` path with 25 generated browser subscriptions and a real local HTTPS push-service fixture. `web-push` performed payload encryption and issued 25 HTTPS requests; the observed peak was **12** concurrent requests. The fixture returned 23×201, 1×410, and 1×404; the broadcast returned all 25 results and persisted 23 subscriptions after cleanup. A one-day self-signed fixture certificate was used with TLS verification disabled only for this local loopback proof.
- `oxfmt --check src/infra/push-web.ts src/infra/push-web.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

AI-assisted: implementation and review were performed with coding agents. A local `codex review --base origin/main` attempt could not start because the configured provider credential (`MYAPI_API_KEY`) is unavailable; independent read-only review found no remaining actionable issues.
